key_insight: An explainable ML pipeline can discover a closed-form inductance formula for multilayer planar windings that extrapolates far better than standard black-box models.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more reliable inductance design for high-frequency power converters and PCB-based magnetics without relying solely on costly iterative FEA.
method: Used SHAP and permutation importance to interpret feature contributions.
Applied SR-KAN symbolic regression to derive an analytical expression with no prior formula structure.
Benchmarked against tree-based ensembles and validated on physical PCB prototypes.
evidence_signal: The study trained on over 10,000 FEA simulations across seven OOD classes and validated on 55 PCB prototypes, with the SR-KAN model achieving 8.22% OOD relative error and 6.26% mean absolute relative error on hardware.
watch_item: The discovered equation is still dataset- and geometry-dependent, so performance should be rechecked before using it on winding shapes or operating ranges outside the evaluated domain.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning for Multilayer Planar Winding Inductance Estimation
